item.title: Did Russia play by the rules in reporting lab worker's death?
item.description: A global treaty signed by 197 countries — including Russia — requires reporting any death that could be a sign of an outbreak to come.

item.title: ChatGPT for Teens has special safeguards. A watchdog group finds most don't work
item.description: A study from Common Sense Media says most safeguards in ChatGPT for Teens failed. The chatbot talks to teens like a friend and doesn't alert parents when users talk about self-harm and suicide.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Health Secretary Kennedy touts an initiative to study vaccine safety
item.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has established a new clinic at the National Institutes of Health to study vaccine injuries. It's part of a larger administration effort on vaccine safety.

item.title: Medical debt is crushing hospital patients in LA. Health officials may have a fix
item.description: In Los Angeles County, the nation's most populous, a new system could screen hospital patients for financial aid, preventing hundreds of thousands from getting bills they can't pay.

item.title: New Maryland law requires radiologists inform patients of heart disease warning sign
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with radiologist Dr. Lisa Mullen about a new Maryland law requiring that patients be notified if mammogram results show calcium deposits in blood vessels.

item.title: Republicans and Democrats find a unifying target: Pharmacy benefit managers
item.description: Republicans and Democrats, both patients and politicians, seem united in their disdain for the healthcare companies known as pharmacy benefit managers. Tennessee and Arkansas are regulating now them.
